thread:
Calcite Support: hey team, Calcite Pay just reported a surge of 429s from their checkout integration, started ~09:12 UTC, affecting ~30% of transactions. customer says it looks like RPM/TMP throttling. can we triage? :frowning_face:
Marta: thanks for flagging. do we have a request id or example trace? any request headers from the client?
Calcite Support: i grabbed one curl from their logs:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-calcite-prod-***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"pay 45.00 to vendor x"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120rpm
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 167
```
response body: `{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "global rpm quota hit" }`
```
Calcite Support: they say traffic pattern is a mix of mobile SDKs and a nightly batch that runs more frequently after a deploy. they only started seeing errors after a vendor deploy yesterday.
Samir: ok that's helpful. header shows an RPM window (120rpm) and remaining 0. looks like they hit a token bucket. do we know whether the failing paths are the same route/model or many different endpoints?
Calcite Support: mostly /v1/generate. a few /v1/embeddings but <5%.
Marta: quick checklist i want run while eng looks deeper: 1) confirm client retries are exponential + jitter 2) check if client rotated keys or created multiple short-lived keys (causes multiple small buckets) 3) ask for sample timestamps for the spike window.
Devon: i'll pull their API key usage from logs, give me ~5m.
ops-bot: started log query job: query=logs:tail source=api-gateway customer=calcite-prod window=+30m
Ryan: small tip — if they run a batch at the same time mobile traffic spikes (deploy related), the aggregate instantaneous RPS can overshoot RPM-based buckets even if average is fine. token bucket resets at windows in some infra config.
Samir: i'm also checking if our gateway has the per-customer burst allowance configured. some plans have a short burst buffer (measured in tokens) on top of RPM. if that buffer is exhausted subsequent requests see 429 until refill.
Marta: Calcite Support, can you ask them if their client uses tight retry loops (no backoff) after a 429? that worsens the collapse.
Calcite Support: they confirmed mobile had immediate retry with fixed 1s interval for 3 attempts. nightly batch has parallelism=20 and no app-level jitter.
Marta: ack. that explains it. parallel batch + tight retries will flatten the client token bucket quickly.
Devon: pulling their key stats now. snippet from gateway logs (redacted):
```
[2026-06-18T09:12:14Z] key=ak_calcite_prod pid=gw-4 req_id=rf3k3  path=/v1/generate status=200 rt=120ms
[2026-06-18T09:12:20Z] key=ak_calcite_prod pid=gw-4 req_id=rf3k9  path=/v1/generate status=429 rt=5ms detail=rate_limit_exceeded
[2026-06-18T09:12:21Z] key=ak_calcite_prod pid=gw-4 req_id=rf3ka  path=/v1/generate status=429 rt=4ms detail=rate_limit_exceeded
[2026-06-18T09:12:24Z] key=ak_calcite_prod pid=gw-4 req_id=rf3kb  path=/v1/generate status=200 rt=110ms
```
Devon: you can see bursts of 429s interleaved with successful requests — classic token-bucket spikes.
Samir: two action tracks: immediate mitigation for production customer, and medium-term client guidance + infra tuning.
Marta: immediate mitigations?
Samir: options:
- advise Calcite to add exponential backoff with full-jitter on 429s (e.g., backoff = random_between(0, base * 2^attempt)) and cap concurrency from batch jobs.
- temporarily increase their RPM quota or burst buffer on our side (requires support tier + config change).
- recommend they stagger nightly batch windows (use cron jitter) and reduce parallelism.
Marta: i'm happy to coordinate a temporary quota bump if legal/finance ok. Calcite is on mid-market plan — need approval.
Oncall: do we have an emergency path for '+short lived burst increase' for customers during deploys?
Ryan: yes, ops can flip a per-key burst flag for up to 30 minutes. it adds +200 tokens burst. requires manual support ticket with approval.
Calcite Support: can we do that now? they are seeing failed checkouts.
Marta: i'll spin up a ticket to ProdOps and mark high priority. also sending client best-practices now.
Marta: Calcite — pls implement client-side fixes asap: 1) add jittered exponential retry 2) reduce batch parallelism from 20 -> 4 for the nightly job and add random stagger between job runs 3) instrument and sample response headers (X-RateLimit-*) so we can correlate.
Calcite Support: sharing quick patch they applied to the batch (node):
```js
// reduced parallelism and jitter
const batchParallel = 4;
await Promise.all(chunks.map(async c => {
  await sleep(Math.random() * 3000);
  return callAPI(c);
}));
```
Calcite Support: they patched mobile retry too (added jitter + cap). they will observe for 20m.
ops-bot: log query finished. summary: 09:10-09:18 window had average 140rpm with 30s spikes to ~800rpm due to parallelism from batch + retries.
Samir: 800rpm instantaneous spike explains 429s against a 120rpm steady-limit; bumping burst would only mask if spikes are short.
Marta: update from ProdOps — temporary burst increase applied for 30m for key ak_calcite_prod. please monitor.
Calcite Support: patch deployed and initial observations: 429 rate dropped from 28% -> ~2% within 2 minutes. mobile clients still occasional 429s but mobile team is rolling patch soon. :thumbsup:
Ryan: medium term recommendations we should send in writing:
- instrument per-route rate limit headers and expose to customers in dashboard. (makes it easier to detect approaching limits)
- publish best-practice doc for batch jobs (prefer staggered starts, concurrency caps, backoff patterns)
- provide a 'burst-test' sim tool so customers can safely test batch intensity.
Samir: infra note for follow-up: review default burst token config and consider auto-burst for customers that pass a rollout healthcheck (small security/abuse risk, but better UX). file: INFRA-642.
Devon: logging note — we should include current token-bucket state in 429 bodies for enterprise customers (exact remaining/next-reset), to avoid blind retries.
Marta: Calcite Support — can you confirm the customer is happy with the temporary increase and the client patches?
Calcite Support: they confirmed, will watch for next 2 deploy cycles. thanks for quick help.
Marta: closing loop: will follow up with a short postmortem to Calcite summarizing cause, short-term actions (burst increase) and long-term suggestions. adding action items: 1) support writeup for temporary burst path 2) internal RFC for per-route headers in 429 bodies 3) customer-facing best-practices doc.
Oncall: marking incident resolved but keeping watch for 4h. :white_check_mark:
Samir: thanks everyone. i'll add a short replay analysis: replayed 1 hour of calcite traffic against staging with the previous batch config to reproduce. attaching results to ticket.
Marta: great, thx. if they rehit limits after next deploy we'll reopen and consider a quota tier upgrade.
Calcite Support: thanks y'all — appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
